newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to continue importing natgas - Reyes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to continue importing natgas - Reyes.

text.p: Mexico will continue to import natural gas from its northwest border, even amid increased production of the fuel, Energy Minister Jesus Reyes Heroles said on Thursday.
Mexico imports the fuel along its northwest border, while exports through Texas at its northeast border, near its most lucrative non-associated gas sites.

"For efficiency and environmental purposes the imports are necessary, whether or not we are self-sufficient," Reyes said at the inauguration of an "Opportunities in Natural Gas Distribution" conference.
But years of Mexico being a net importer of natural gas, largely from the United States, could soon change, he added.
"In 1997 we will probably have a small surplus, even with Cactus not fully recovered and higher local gas demand," Reyes said.

An explosion at the key natural gas processing Cactus complex in July required a boost in Mexico's exports of the fuel for months. The government has said it should be at full capacity by July, although as of February it was still at half its former output levels.

Mexico has surged its natural gas exploration activity to prepare for an anticipated leap in demand for the fuel in coming years. Analysts estimate Mexico's natural gas demand should be the highest in the region, with government estimates predicting current consumption will double by 2005 to about 7.16 billion cubic feet.
As part of a boost in natural gas exploration activity begun this year, Mexico's Burgos Basin should produce 1.4 billion cubic feet per day (cfd) by 2001, from a current 470 million cfd, Reyes said.
The nation's richest hydrocarbon field, Cantarell in Campeche Sound, should produce 900 million cfd by 2000 as a result of expansion there, he added.
